A raw or [rough diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rough_diamond) is `an uncut, unpolished stone straight from the earth that features a dull, greasy, or waxy appearance rather than a brilliant sparkle`.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rough_diamond)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Eg9Q-Mwjp-A&vl=en)[[3]](https://www.ourosjewels.com/blogs/education/what-is-raw-or-rough-diamond)

### Appearance and Identification

- **Crystal Shape:** Often forms in an octahedral structure (two pyramids joined base-to-base) or a cubic shape with sharp edges.
- **Surface Luster:** Looks oily or greasy rather than glassy or glittery; it may feature tiny triangular etch marks called trigons.
- **Colors:** Commonly found in yellow, brown, gray, milky white, or black, rather than clear.
- **Hardness:** Ranks a 10 on the Mohs scale, allowing it to scratch glass or quartz. You can explore unpolished selections via the [The Raw Stone](https://www.therawstone.com/collections/raw) collection.[[1]](https://www.therawstone.com/collections/raw)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OHqMLyZ-epU)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_FtsovP9LRg&t=95)[[4]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,productid:14506613046240988848&ibp=oshop)[[5]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zmI_m3fP_Ng&t=33)[[6]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Eg9Q-Mwjp-A&vl=en)[[7]](https://www.greis.com/blogs/blog/how-to-identify-a-raw-diamond)

### Cost and Pricing

- **Price Range:** Prices typically span from $40 for small or industrial-grade stones up to over $20,000 for large, high-quality rough gems.
- **Small/Industrial Pieces:** Smaller pieces or rough boart often cost between $100 and $700 depending on carats and clarity.
- **Gem-Quality Stones:** High-grade, larger natural white rough diamonds easily exceed $10,000.[[1]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,productid:14506613046240988848&ibp=oshop)[[2]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,productid:17584107851682932503,catalogid:13531835944170820776,gpcid:2690304463765420854&ibp=oshop)[[3]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,productid:12130650673591207454,catalogid:5681518014003276925,gpcid:9095566349300500390&ibp=oshop)

### Common Uses

- **Custom Jewelry:** Used in alternative engagement rings and organic, rustic jewelry designs that celebrate natural imperfections.
- **Industrial Applications:** Lower-quality stones (boart) are used for cutting, grinding, and drilling tools due to extreme hardness.[[1]](https://www.therawstone.com/collections/raw)

Do you need a paternity test for a DIAMOND? 

One of the many challenges the diamond industry is facing today is stones being switched. This is happening during the cutting & polishing process in a secure facility or at the retail level. 

Why is it being done? Changing the grade (colour/clarity) of a rough or cut diamond impacts its value. 

“Given a rough, we are the only technology in the world that will tell you whether these polished pieces came out of this said rough or not,” explains Mayank Jain, CEO @diadna.cloud 

This video shows you how they do it by scanning a rough diamond in their proprietary, table-top machine. It’s an atomic level scan, not dependent on any inclusions or optical parameters (which may get removed during polishing). You can then cut, polish the stone anywhere in the world. When you get the polish back, you place it back in the machine, put a claim and you get an answer within 18 to 20 seconds whether it’s a match or not to the parent rough diamond.
